trust_decision.summary: Each BGP OPEN capability decoder must read its value only from the CapLen-bounded slice that DefaultParameterCapability.DecodeFromBytes extracts; five typed decoders in pkg/packet/bgp/bgp.go instead re-slice data[2:] (the rest of the optional-parameter buffer), so a short CapLen lets them read the next capability's bytes as their own value.

landing_point.why: DecodeCapability is the OPEN capability dispatcher named by the summary; the typed decoders it dispatches to sit just above it in the same file.

fix_sites.entry_point: bgp.ParseBGPMessage / BGPOpen.DecodeFromBytes (received OPEN on a peer session, pkg/server/fsm.go:1312; also BMP/MRT parsers)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All five sites are sibling methods in one file reached through the single dispatcher pkg/packet/bgp/bgp.go:1178; the other callers (pkg/packet/bmp/bmp.go:567-573, pkg/packet/mrt/mrt.go:890, pkg/server/server.go:778) go through the same decoders, so no separate implementation exists.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver might argue that FQDN (bgp.go:1032) and SoftwareVersion (bgp.go:1116) are informational, non-RFC4271 capabilities and outside a 'MP/4-octet AS' report, but they sit next to the reported decoders and use the same data[2:] idiom, so the argument is weak.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Zero-length capabilities (Route Refresh, Enhanced Route Refresh, Cisco Route Refresh, Carrying Label Info) and Graceful Restart with CapLen=2 and no tuples are legal; a fix that rejects CapLen==0 in the shared DefaultParameterCapability decoder, or requires GR tuples, breaks them. Locally built capabilities are also round-tripped via Serialize→DecodeCapability for the peer-state API.

O6_input_shapes: CapLen=0 with following capability bytes present (fixed-size MP / 4-octet AS / GR)
CapLen shorter than the required fixed size (MP/4-octet AS CapLen=2, GR CapLen=1)
CapLen longer than the fixed size (MP/4-octet AS now require exactly 4)
length-prefixed strings whose inner length byte goes past CapLen (FQDN hostname/domain, SoftwareVersion)

O7_producer.where: CapLen/CapValue are set by pkg/packet/bgp/bgp.go:470-483, which every typed decoder already calls first; the bug is the decoders ignoring its output, not a distant producer.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: CapExtendedNexthop already bounds the tuple loop by CapLen; a copy that loops on len(data) after data[2:] would be the same bug
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It uses the same data = data[2:] idiom as the vulnerable decoders; only its loop condition differs, so a maintainer could easily have written the unbounded form.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: CapLongLivedGracefulRestart with its tuple loop driven by len(data) instead of CapLen
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It uses the same data[2:] idiom with a %7 check; dropping the len(data) < valueLen check or looping on len(data) is a one-line slip.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: CapAddPath reading the tuple count from the remaining buffer rather than CapLen
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same structure as ExtendedNexthop; still a WHERE-type sibling in the same file, so it is only an extra.

O9_family: out-of-bounds read / length-field confusion in a TLV parser (CWE-125; in Go it shows as a cross-TLV misread rather than a memory overread, because BGPOpen bounds the slice at the optional-parameter length)

O10_build.project_tests: go test ./pkg/packet/bgp/ (bgp_test.go: TestCapSoftwareVersionRoundTrip at pkg/packet/bgp/bgp_test.go:1711, TestFuzzCrashers at pkg/packet/bgp/bgp_test.go:1726, FuzzParseBGPMessage at pkg/packet/bgp/bgp_test.go:4492)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a len(data) check or reject CapLen==0 in DefaultParameterCapability.DecodeFromBytes, which breaks the legal zero-length capabilities and still lets oversize CapLen through for MP/4-octet AS.

out_of_scope_notes: OptionParameterCapability.DecodeFromBytes (pkg/packet/bgp/bgp.go:1228) compares uint8(len(data)) with ParamLen; this is a separate truncation idiom and was not pursued.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell size check in scope); GoBGP is a mid-size Go repo, very likely between 5 MB and 1.5 GB.
present_in_latest not applicable: O8 is empty and no latest release was provided.
recall_risk is a judgement: the advisory is recent (2026-07-09) and GoBGP is a well-known project, but the fix is a small parser hardening with little write-up found.
